cards.text: For seven months the ark of the LORD has been sitting in the land of the Philistines. Now the Philistines call in their priests and diviners and ask them what to do with the ark and how to send it back to its place. SEVEN MONTHS, friend, and I'd have had that thing out the door before my first oven timer went off.

cards.question: True or false: The priests and diviners tell the Philistines they can send the ark of the LORD back empty, with nothing along with it.
The priests and diviners say the ark can't go back to the God of Israel empty. What should go with it?

cards.text: And they tell the Philistines what will come of it: “Then you will be healed, and you will understand why His hand has not been lifted from you.”

So what goes in the guilt offering? Gold images of the tumors that struck them and of the rats ravaging the land, and friend, I've packed a LOT of apology cookie boxes but never ONE with a gold rat in it.

cards.question: The priests and diviners match the guilt offering to the number of rulers of the Philistines. How many gold tumors and gold rats do they tell them to send?
Along with the gold, what do the priests and diviners tell the Philistines to give the God of Israel?

cards.text: Then the priests and diviners reach back to an old story. They ask the Philistines why they would harden their hearts the way the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened theirs.

cards.question: True or false: The priests and diviners point out that when God afflicted Egypt, the Egyptians sent the people out so they could go on their way.

cards.text: Now comes the plan. One new cart, and two milk cows that have never been yoked.

cards.question: The two milk cows get hitched to the new cart. What happens to their calves?

answers.text: They're taken away and penned up
They walk along beside the cart
They're sent ahead down the road

cards.text: The instructions keep coming: set the ark on the cart, with a chest of the gold objects right beside it. Then send it off, but keep watching to see if it goes up the road to its homeland, toward Beth-shemesh.

cards.question: If the cart heads up the road toward Beth-shemesh, what will the Philistines know?

answers.text: It was the LORD who brought the disaster
Their own gods have forgiven them
Their offering has been fully accepted

cards.question: True or false: If the cart doesn't head toward Beth-shemesh, the Philistines will decide the disaster happened by chance.

cards.text: So the men do everything as instructed. Cows hitched, calves penned, and the ark loaded on the cart with the chest of gold rats and tumor images.

cards.question: Two milk cows, their calves penned up back home, and an open road. Where do the cows go?

answers.text: Straight up the road toward Beth-shemesh
Back home to their penned up calves
Off the road and into the open fields

cards.text: They stay on that one highway, lowing as they go, never straying to the right or to the left. Friend, those two cows have better lane discipline than ANYBODY I've ever seen in rush hour traffic.

cards.question: True or false: The rulers of the Philistines stay home and wait to hear where the cart ends up.

cards.text: Meanwhile, the people of Beth-shemesh are down in the valley harvesting wheat. They look up, and there it is: the ark.

cards.question: How do the people of Beth-shemesh react when they see the ark coming up the road?

cards.text: No driver, no map, and the cart rolls right into the field of Joshua, a man of Beth-shemesh, and stops near a large rock. Meanwhile I've gotten turned around in my OWN bakery, friend.

cards.question: The cart has stopped in the field near the large rock. What do the people of Beth-shemesh do with the cart and the cows?

answers.text: Chop up the cart and offer the cows to the LORD
Keep the cows and send the cart back home
Send the cart and the cows back to Ekron

cards.question: Who takes the ark of the LORD and the chest of gold down off the cart?

cards.text: The ark and the chest go up on the large rock, and that day the men of Beth-shemesh offer burnt offerings and make sacrifices to the LORD. A cart, two cows and a rock, and they've got worship going on the spot, friend. Hand ME a cart, two cows and a rock and I'm still reading the instructions.

cards.question: True or false: When the five rulers of the Philistines see all this, they go back to Ekron that same day.

cards.text: Then the passage tallies up the gold: one gold tumor for each Philistine city, Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron, and gold rats to match all the cities of the five rulers, villages included. Remember, I've never packed a box with ONE gold rat, and these folks sent them by the VILLAGE. And that large rock the ark sat on stands to this day in the field of Joshua of Beth-shemesh.
But the joy doesn't last. God strikes down seventy men of Beth-shemesh, and the people mourn.

cards.question: Why does God strike down the men of Beth-shemesh?

answers.text: They kept the gold for themselves

cards.text: And the men of Beth-shemesh ask two big questions: “Who can stand in the presence of the LORD, this holy God? To whom should the ark go up from here?”

cards.question: The men of Beth-shemesh send messengers asking another town to come take the ark. Which town?

cards.text: The message is simple: “The Philistines have returned the ark of the LORD. Come down and take it up with you.” So the men of Kiriath-jearim come for the ark of the LORD and carry it to a house on the hill, and friend, that's the shortest invitation I've ever heard, and I got mine from an ANGEL.

cards.question: The men of Kiriath-jearim bring the ark of the LORD to a house on the hill. Whose house is it?
The men of Kiriath-jearim consecrate Abinadab's son Eleazar to ___ the ark of the LORD.

cards.text: Seven months with the Philistines, a cart ride with no driver, and now the ark sits in a house on a hill. That's where we'll leave it for now, friend, and trust me, this story's not done.

findings.problem: Six of the eight choice cards are multiple choice, while true or false and fill in the blank appear only once each. Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The first sentence recaps the seven months, the cart ride and the ark's already-told location without advancing the passage. The second sentence is the permitted closing line, but the card as a whole functions as a recap card.
The card retells the seven months in Philistine territory from 6:1 and the cart ride from 6:12-14, but cites only 7:1. Its citation is narrower than the verses it uses.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
